newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: FEDERAL LIBERAL PARTY MEETING BEGINS IN HOBART
Federal Liberal M-P's will have a reprieve from the pressure of the Opposition over the ministerial shareholding debarcle today, when they attend their Party's Federal Council meeting in Hobart.
It's the first Federal Council meeting since the Liberals came to office, and follows what has arguably been their toughest week in government so far.
Prime Minister John Howard will attend the meeting along with senior federal front benchers, state premiers and party presidents. Offer not to claim Native title over mine
MIM SAYS NOT THREATENED BY LAND CLAIM
The director of an MIM mining company in north-west Queensland says he's not threatened by the possibility of having a Native title claim lodged over his Ernest Henry Mine.
John Loraine says his company has dismissed an alleged proposal by an Aboriginal Corporation not to lodge a Native Title claim over the mine site, in return for 120 million dollars.
Ernest Henry Mining Company director John Loraine says the offer, from the Mitakoodi Junjlar Aboriginal Corporation has no legal foundation, and is unacceptable.
It's alleged that in return for the compensation for land use, there would be no Native Title claim interference to the mine or to the supply of power or water.
But spokesman for the Corporation, Charles Perkins, has denied that any offer at all was made to MIM.
ACTU SENT $89,300 BILL FOR PARLIAMENT RIOT DAMAGE
The Australian Council of Trade Unions has been sent a bill for the damage caused to Parliament House in Canberra during demonstrations on the 19th and 20th of August.
The ACT Government has sent an account for $89,300 to ACTU President Jennie George.
ACT Police Minister Gary Humphries says he expects that figure to rise when criminal injuries compensation payments are made to police officers injured during the demonstrations.
Mr Humphries says he fully expects the ACTU to pay the bill as it and the affiliated ACT Trades and Labour Council were responsible for organising the rally.
SWEDISH TENOR ARRIVES FOR AUSTRALIAN TOUR
Legendary Swedish tenor Nicolai Gedda has arrived today to begin his first concert tour of Australia ... at the age of 71.
He's currently touring Asia, where he has been winning standing ovations at each performance.
Gedda has made more than 200 recordings ... and is considered an operatic superstar even among the popular Three Tenors.
He's particularly won acclaim for his command of nine languages and a huge variety of musical styles.
Gedda's tour will begin in Melbourne and include Sydney, Adelaide and Brisbane.
CODE OF PRACTICE FOR BUILDERS TO BE DISCUSSED
A national code of practice for Australia's 50-billion dollar construction and building industry will be discussed at a meeting of Commonwealth, State and Territory ministers in Adelaide today.
The proposed code will focus on clients rights, relationships, tendering, occupational health and safety and industrial reforms.
South Australia's State Services Minister, Wayne Matthew, says a collaborative effort is needed by Government to ensure the industry's development.
Ministers are also likely to endorse a strategy for the long term improvement of security of payments in the industry.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
